items.intendedText: The ocean has different layers. Near the surface, there is plenty of sunlight and warmth. Further down, it grows colder and darker. Below 200 metres, no sunlight reaches at all.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Under the Ocean
items.intendedText: The top layer is full of life. Coral reefs grow in warm, shallow water. They are home to thousands of kinds of fish and animal. A coral reef is like an underwater city.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Under the Ocean
items.intendedText: Coral looks like rock or plant, but it is an animal. Each piece of coral is made of thousands of tiny creatures called polyps. Coral reefs take thousands of years to grow.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Under the Ocean
items.intendedText: Further down, in the deep and dark, strange creatures live. Many have enormous eyes to see in the dim light. Some are found nowhere else on Earth.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Under the Ocean
items.intendedText: In the deepest, darkest water, some creatures make their own light. This is called bioluminescence. The anglerfish dangles a glowing lure to attract prey.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Under the Ocean
items.intendedText: The deepest part of the ocean is called the Mariana Trench. It is nearly 11 kilometres deep. If you put the world's tallest mountain inside it, it would still be covered by water.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Under the Ocean
items.intendedText: The ocean makes more than half the oxygen we breathe. Tiny plants called phytoplankton float near the surface. They use sunlight to make oxygen. Every other breath you take came from the ocean.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Under the Ocean
items.intendedText: More than 80% of the ocean has never been explored. We know more about the surface of the Moon than we do about the deep ocean. There is so much left to discover.

items.title: Butterflies
items.intendedText: Butterflies are insects. Like all insects, they have six legs, four wings, and a body in three parts. They also have two long antennae.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Butterflies
items.intendedText: A butterfly's life has four stages. This is called a lifecycle. Each stage looks completely different from the one before.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Butterflies
items.intendedText: Stage one: the butterfly lays tiny eggs on a leaf. The eggs are very small — some are no bigger than a pinhead. The leaf is food for the caterpillar inside.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Butterflies
items.intendedText: Stage two: the egg hatches into a caterpillar. The caterpillar's only job is to eat. It eats and eats and grows and grows. Some caterpillars eat their own eggshell first!
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Butterflies
items.intendedText: Stage three: the caterpillar makes a hard shell around itself. This is called a chrysalis. Inside, an extraordinary change is about to happen.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Butterflies
items.intendedText: Inside the chrysalis, the caterpillar breaks down completely. Its body rebuilds itself as a butterfly. This amazing process is called metamorphosis. It takes one to two weeks.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Butterflies
items.intendedText: Stage four: the butterfly pushes out of the chrysalis. Its wings are wet and crumpled. The butterfly hangs still and waits. Slowly, its wings unfurl and dry.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Butterflies
items.intendedText: Butterflies drink nectar from flowers. They find flowers using their eyes and sense of smell. But they taste with their feet! Standing on a flower tells them if it is good to eat.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Butterflies
items.intendedText: Some butterflies migrate thousands of kilometres. The monarch butterfly flies from Canada to Mexico every year — a journey of 4,000 kilometres. They always find the same trees.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Caves
items.intendedText: Caves are hollow spaces underground or inside cliffs. They form in many different ways. Some are made by water, some by sea waves, and some by ancient flowing lava.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Caves
items.intendedText: Most caves form when rainwater seeps into limestone rock. The water is slightly acidic. It slowly dissolves the rock away. This takes thousands and thousands of years.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Caves
items.intendedText: Over time, tunnels and chambers form underground. Some cave systems stretch for hundreds of kilometres. The Mammoth Cave system in America has more than 650 kilometres of passages.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Caves
items.intendedText: Water drips from cave ceilings for thousands of years. The minerals in the water build up slowly. These hanging stone shapes are called stalactites. They form one tiny drip at a time.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Caves
items.intendedText: When drips hit the cave floor, minerals build up there too. These rising stone shapes are called stalagmites. They grow just a few centimetres every hundred years.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Caves
items.intendedText: When a stalactite and a stalagmite meet, they form a column. A cave column can take tens of thousands of years to grow. Each one is unique.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Caves
items.intendedText: Caves are home to many animals. Bats sleep hanging upside down from cave ceilings by day. At dusk, thousands of bats fly out together to feed on insects in the night air.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Caves
items.intendedText: Some creatures live only in caves and never come out. Over thousands of years, they have adapted. Cave fish are often pale or white — they have never needed colour. Many have no eyes at all.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Caves
items.intendedText: Long ago, people lived in caves. They painted pictures on the cave walls. Cave paintings have been found that are more than 40,000 years old. The artists were humans just like us.

items.title: Frogs
items.intendedText: Frogs are amphibians. Amphibians can live in water and on land. Frogs begin their life in water and later move onto land.

items.title: Frogs
items.intendedText: A female frog lays hundreds of eggs in water. The eggs are called frogspawn. Each egg is surrounded by clear jelly that protects it and keeps it safe.

items.title: Frogs
items.intendedText: After a few weeks, tadpoles wriggle out of the eggs. Tadpoles have tails and no legs. They breathe underwater using gills, like fish.

items.title: Frogs
items.intendedText: Slowly, the tadpole changes. Back legs appear first. Then front legs. The tail shrinks away. After about twelve weeks, it is a frog!
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Frogs
items.intendedText: The young frog climbs out of the water. It can now breathe air through its lungs. It can also live on land. The whole world opens up.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Frogs
items.intendedText: Frogs are expert hunters. They have long, sticky tongues. A frog can flip its tongue out and back in less time than a blink to catch an insect.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Frogs
items.intendedText: A frog's skin is always damp. Frogs can breathe through their skin as well as through their lungs. They must never dry out.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Frogs
items.intendedText: Frogs come in amazing colours. Bright colours are a warning: I am poisonous — do not eat me! The more colourful the frog, often the more dangerous it is.

items.title: Frogs
items.intendedText: Frogs sing to find a mate. Each species has its own call. The ribbit of a tree frog, the deep croak of a bullfrog — their calls fill warm evenings around the world.

items.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
items.intendedText: Dad had been talking about the castle trip since January. A proper medieval castle, forty minutes away — with a tower you could actually climb, a dungeon that was a real dungeon, and a great hall whose stone floor had been there for six hundred years. items.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
items.intendedText: They drove there on a bright Saturday in April. Aiden pressed his face to the car window when the castle appeared over the hill — grey stone towers above the treeline, impossibly old and very much still there. He felt something he didn't yet have a word for.

items.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
items.intendedText: The entrance was a proper drawbridge — working, over a real water-filled moat. It was smaller than he'd imagined and more real than he'd imagined. items.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
items.intendedText: The great hall was vast and grey and cool. The stone floor was uneven and worn in paths where feet had walked for centuries. Aiden crouched and pressed his hand flat to the floor. Six hundred years of footsteps had passed here. He could not quite hold that thought all at once.

items.title: Aiden and Betty and the Castle
items.intendedText: The North Tower had one hundred and twelve steps. They counted every one, out loud, all together. The staircase was so narrow they had to go single file. At the top: the whole landscape, the river, the town, a motorway miles away. The same view and entirely different.

items.title: The Night the Stars Fell
items.intendedText:
Stone raised their hands high.
Pip and Spark added a little push.
The star spirits lifted.
Up.
And up.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Night the Stars Fell
items.intendedText:
The star spirits went up.
Slowly at first.
Then faster.
One by one they found their places.
The sky filled back up with stars.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Night the Stars Fell
items.intendedText:
The last star spirit sat in Stone's hand.
It blinked its large gold eyes at everyone.
"See you next year," it said.
Then it bounced once.
Then it went up.
Then it was gone.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
items.intendedText:
It was late in the Hollow Oak.
Everyone was asleep.
Then Pip heard it.
Scratch.
Shuffle.
A tiny voice: "...where DID I put them..."
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
items.intendedText:
Pip woke Wren.
They listened together.
Scratch.
Shuffle.
"...they were right here..."
"Something is in the walls," said Wren.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
items.intendedText:
By morning, everyone knew.
They stood outside the Hollow Oak.
"It makes those sounds," said Luna.
"It always has."
"It HAS?" said everyone.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
items.intendedText:
Pip, Wren, Burrow, and Fern went inside to search.
They searched every room.
They found nothing.
Then Burrow's nose twitched.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
items.intendedText:
"There is a room here," said Burrow.
He found a small door near the roots.
It was very small.
Too small for most of them.
"I can go," said Fern.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
items.intendedText:
Fern went through the small door.
She was inside for a moment.
Then she called back:
"There is someone here."
Everyone pressed their ears to the door.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
items.intendedText:
Inside was a room.
It was small and warm.
It was full of collected things.
A tiny creature was searching through them.
She did not look up.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
items.intendedText:
"Hello," said Fern.
The tiny creature looked up.
"Have you seen my spectacles?" she said.
"I've been looking for three days."
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
items.intendedText:
Fern looked around the room.
Then she looked at Twig.
The spectacles were on top of Twig's head.
They had been there all along.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
items.intendedText:
"I am Twig," said the tiny creature.
"I live here."
"I have always lived here."
She seemed perfectly happy about this.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
items.intendedText:
Fern came back through the door.
"Her name is Twig," said Fern.
"She has lived here for many years."
Everyone looked at Luna.
"Of course," said Luna.
"Twig."
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Something Lives in the Hollow Oak
items.intendedText:
They made Twig a slightly larger door.
Twig came out for acorn biscuits.
She sat in the big room and looked around.
"I like it here," she said.
"But I like my room better."
"This is also very nice."
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Big Moonwood Race
items.intendedText: The Big Moonwood Race
items.qaNotes: Released for student Guided Reading from complete Moonwood Tales Level C books 11-25 source pack. Cover uses story page 1 art because no separate cover file was delivered.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Big Moonwood Race
items.intendedText:
Luna read out the race rules.
The course: from the Hollow Oak to the Crystal Stream to the Tumblerock Cliffs and back.
Everyone was at the starting line.
Everyone was ready.
Mostly.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Big Moonwood Race
items.intendedText:
They were off.
Pip ran.
Fern flew.
Stone trotted.
Dewdrop glided.
Wren ran and read her spell book.
Flint took a very confident turn left.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Big Moonwood Race
items.intendedText:
Flint went left.
Then left again.
Then the Fog Marsh was ahead of him.
"I am taking a scenic route," said Flint.
There was no one to hear him.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Big Moonwood Race
items.intendedText:
Wren found a speed spell.
She cast it.
It worked on everyone near her.
Everyone shot forward very fast.
Except Wren.
She watched them all go.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Big Moonwood Race
items.intendedText:
Glimmer could not stop.
Glimmer hit Spark.
Sparkles went everywhere.
They both kept moving.
Very fast.
In new directions.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Big Moonwood Race
items.intendedText:
Stone hit a root.
Stone began to fall.
This took a while.
Stone was very large.
Stone fell slowly.
Magnificently.
Like a small cliff sitting down.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Big Moonwood Race
items.intendedText:
Pip reached the Crystal Stream.
He leaped from stone to stone.
One stone was slippery.
Pip went in.
He came out the other side.
Still running.
Very wet.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Big Moonwood Race
items.intendedText:
Halfway through, everyone was somewhere different.
Pip was wet.
Stone was standing up again.
Spark had lost his hat.
Flint was not visible.
Wren was still walking.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Big Moonwood Race
items.intendedText:
Dewdrop crossed the finish line.
She had glided the whole way.
She was not wet.
She was not ruffled.
"Finished," said Dewdrop.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Big Moonwood Race
items.intendedText:
Everyone finished.
Eventually.
Pip was still damp.
Spark had found his hat.
Stone had found a bruise.
Flint arrived from the wrong direction.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Big Moonwood Race
items.intendedText:
Luna counted everyone.
Everyone was back.
Then there was a rumbling.
Burrow came up through the ground.
Right beside the finish line.
He did not look tired.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Big Moonwood Race
items.intendedText:
Dewdrop won a gold leaf for finishing.
Burrow won a gold leaf for best route.
"I did not win," said Flint.
"You went to the Fog Marsh," said Pip.
"I saw many things," said Flint.
He was already drawing them.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
items.intendedText: The Fog Marsh Mystery
items.qaNotes: Released for student Guided Reading from complete Moonwood Tales Level C books 11-25 source pack. Cover uses story page 1 art because no separate cover file was delivered.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
items.intendedText:
Pip noticed it on a Tuesday.
The grey fog of the Fog Marsh was closer.
It had never come this near before.
He marked the edge with a stick.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
items.intendedText:
By the end of the week, the fog had crept closer.
The mushrooms at the edge were going out.
One by one.
The fog was not stopping.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
items.intendedText:
Pip told Luna.
Luna listened carefully.
"Something is wrong at the marsh," she said.
"We must go in."
Pip, Fern, and Dewdrop came too.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
items.intendedText:
Inside the marsh, it was colder.
The trees drooped.
The water did not move.
Dewdrop led them through the fog.
She could feel the water.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
items.intendedText:
At the centre of the marsh, they found it.
A figure made of grey mist.
It sat against a dead tree.
It was very still.
It looked very sad.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
items.intendedText:
Dewdrop went close.
"What is wrong?" she asked.
The spirit looked up slowly.
Its eyes were dim.
"My home," it said.
"Every year, smaller."
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
items.intendedText:
The spirit pointed to the edges.
They looked.
There were things left behind.
A rope.
An old lamp.
A pile of mushroom caps.
Left by Moonwood creatures.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
items.intendedText:
"We didn't know," said Pip.
"We left things without thinking," said Fern.
The spirit looked at them.
"Every year, more things."
"Every year, a little smaller."
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
items.intendedText:
"We'll clear it," said Pip.
"Now," said Fern.
They spent the afternoon clearing the marsh edge.
As they worked, the spirit watched.
Slowly, it began to sit up.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
items.intendedText:
When the edge was clear, the spirit stood.
Its shape was clearer now.
"Thank you," said the spirit.
It was not mist anymore.
It was something more solid.
Something more itself.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
items.intendedText:
They marked the boundary at the Hollow Oak.
Everyone placed a stone.
"The marsh is the marsh," said Luna.
"Moonwood is Moonwood."
"And we leave space for both."
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: The Fog Marsh Mystery
items.intendedText:
That evening, the fog stayed at the line.
The mushrooms began to come back on.
One by one.
Pip watched them light up.
The marsh was where it should be.
The forest was where it should be.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
items.intendedText: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
items.qaNotes: Released for student Guided Reading from complete Moonwood Tales Level C books 11-25 source pack. Cover uses story page 1 art because no separate cover file was delivered.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
items.intendedText:
There was a sign on the Hollow Oak door.
GLIMMER'S FIRE PERFORMANCE — TODAY.
Everyone came.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
items.intendedText:
They all sat in the clearing.
Glimmer stood at the front.
It was very quiet.
"Ready," said Glimmer.
It did not quite feel true.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
items.intendedText:
Glimmer breathed in.
Deeply.
Glimmer breathed out.
A jet of orange fire came out.
Small.
Perfect.
Real.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
items.intendedText:
Everyone gasped.
Pip covered his mouth.
Stone's eyes went very wide.
Luna took off her glasses and put them back on.
It was real.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
items.intendedText:
Glimmer did it again.
Longer.
The fire was steady.
It was warm.
Glimmer's scales caught the light.
Glimmer had never looked so much like a dragon.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
items.intendedText:
Glimmer got excited.
Glimmer breathed in very deeply.
Much more deeply than before.
Stone took a small step back.
"Glimmer," said Pip.
Glimmer breathed out.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
items.intendedText:
The fire was very large.
It was taller than Glimmer.
It caught the torch on the Hollow Oak door.
The torch lit the first lamp.
The lamp lit a mushroom.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
items.intendedText:
The light spread.
Mushroom to mushroom.
Lamp to lamp.
Through every path.
Through every dark corner of Moonwood.
All of it lighting up.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
items.intendedText:
Moonwood blazed with gold.
Every mushroom.
Every lamp.
Every glowing stone.
The forest was more beautiful than anyone had ever seen it.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
items.intendedText:
Everyone looked at the forest.
Then everyone looked at Glimmer.
Glimmer looked at the forest.
Glimmer looked at their own mouth.
"Oh," said Glimmer.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
items.intendedText:
The fire faded slowly.
Moonwood kept its glow.
Luna looked at Glimmer over her glasses.
"Quite controlled," said Luna.
"Thank you," said Glimmer.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: Glimmer Breathes Fire at Last
items.intendedText:
"I did it," said Glimmer.
"You did," said Pip.
"I'd like to do it again," said Glimmer.
Everyone who heard this took a small step back.
"We know," said everyone.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
items.intendedText: One Night in the Deep Dark
items.qaNotes: Released for student Guided Reading from complete Moonwood Tales Level C books 11-25 source pack. Cover uses story page 1 art because no separate cover file was delivered.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
items.intendedText:
It was the deepest part of the night.
Moonwood was very quiet.
Then there was a sound at the edge of the clearing.
Something small was there.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
items.intendedText:
Pip opened the door.
A small creature was at the edge of the clearing.
It had very large silver eyes.
It was frightened.
It did not run.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
items.intendedText:
Pip knelt down.
He held still.
The creature came closer.
One step.
Then another.
"Hello," said Pip, very quietly.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
items.intendedText:
Pip brought it inside.
Everyone woke up.
Stone brought a piece of acorn biscuit.
The creature ate it very carefully.
It watched everyone with its large silver eyes.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
items.intendedText:
"Where is your home?" asked Burrow, gently.
The creature looked at its paws.
Then at the window.
"Deep," it said.
"Deep dark."
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
items.intendedText:
"We'll take you home," said Pip.
"But the Deep Dark—" said Wren.
"We'll go together," said Pip.
Everyone looked at each other.
"Together," said Stone.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
items.intendedText:
They all went together.
Luna led — her eyes could see in any dark.
Glimmer breathed a small flame for the path.
The creature walked between them.
Into the deep.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
items.intendedText:
The Deep Dark was very dark.
The trees had no glow.
The light went only a little way ahead.
They walked close together.
No one was last.
No one was alone.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
items.intendedText:
Burrow found the underground path.
He could smell the way.
The creature stepped forward.
It knew this place.
"Here," it said.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
items.intendedText:
Beyond the roots, a small clearing.
Silver moss lit the ground.
It was warm.
Other creatures were there.
They looked up.
They had the same enormous silver eyes.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
items.intendedText:
The creature ran to its family.
The family gathered around it.
They looked at the Moonwood creatures.
Not afraid.
Just looking.
Then one of them blinked.
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.

items.title: One Night in the Deep Dark
items.intendedText:
They walked back through the Dark.
At the edge, Pip looked back.
One silver light blinked twice.
"That was brave," said Glimmer.
Pip touched the stone in his pocket.
"Yes," he said. "It ran home."
"That's the bravest kind."
items.action: Keep, but spot-check visually during normal QA.
